citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
Scabbed lesions with noticeable crusting were seen on the distal ear tips of seven wolf-hybrids. Fresh blood was also
present on the left ear flap of one wolf along its outer edge. During the inspection, the wolves intermittently shook their
heads to deter the flies hovering nearby. Though the facility representative stated they’d noticed the lesions yesterday and
planned to contact their veterinarian, the vet hadn’t been contacted by the time of this inspection.
Failure to communicate with the attending veterinarian to relay pertinent information regarding an animal’s condition can
lead to prolonged discomfort, or deterioration of the animal’s health. All animals are to be observed daily to assess their
health and well-being. The facility shall ensure there is a mechanism of direct and frequent communication with the
attending veterinarian so that timely and accurate information on problems of animal health, behavior and well-being are
conveyed.
The facility corrected during the inspection, and to remain corrected from June 9, 2026, forward.

Records of the monthly parasite preventatives administered to seven wolf-hybrids were incomplete on today’s inspection.
The licensee stated they’ve given an oral dewormer monthly to each wolf, but the last recorded dose was dated August 1,
2025. Documented medical records confirm medications were given as outlined in the program of veterinary care and
help ensure that the guidance of the attending veterinarian is being followed. The facility must keep and maintain the
names of all vaccines and treatments and the dates of administration given to the wolf-hybrids at the facility.
Correct by June 14, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
